en.summary: Advertising demand and pricing supported revenue growth, while the legal charge weighed on operating profit and infrastructure cash spending exceeded OCF. EPS growth is amplified by a very high year-ago tax rate. Assess the core advertising engine, Reality Labs losses, legal cash obligations and AI investment separately before drawing conclusions from the headline earnings increase.
findings: Revenue was $64.601B, changing 26.07% YoY. GAAP diluted EPS was $3.83 versus $1.05 a year ago. These are realized standalone results for 2026-07-01–2026-09-30; changes in the business mix and special items need to be evaluated alongside the consolidated comparison.

GAAP operating income was $12.988B. Dividing it by revenue gives an operating margin of about 20.105%, versus 40.075% a year ago. The financial table separately retains GAAP gross margin of 79.305%. Gross and operating margins measure different expense levels; neither measures cash left after capital investment or the return earned on the installed asset base.

OCF was $32.786B. Property purchases of $33.942B plus $964M of finance-lease principal exceeded receipts, producing company-defined FCF of negative $2.120B versus positive $10.625B a year ago. Subtracting property purchases alone would overstate this company measure. Legal expense recognition and settlement payment timing also differ, so the litigation charge is not a proxy for current-quarter cash paid.

Ad impressions rose 10% and average price per ad 14% YoY. Advertising revenue was $63.061B, within Family of Apps revenue of $64.158B. Both volume and pricing support the revenue result, but multiplying rounded growth rates is only an approximation and does not isolate currency, mix or individual-app contributions.

The $9.89B legal charge reduced operating income to $12.988B; the company says EPS excluding it would be $7.40 versus GAAP $3.83. At the same time, the effective tax rate fell to 24% from 87% a year ago. Consequently, the approximately 265% reported EPS increase is not an equivalent growth rate for ongoing advertising operations.

Management expects Q4 revenue of $73B–$76B and 2026 capital spending including lease principal of $135B–$145B. The attorneys-general agreement provides for payments up to approximately $18.59B, beyond the current charge alone. These are separate forecasting and contingent/legal scopes; infrastructure returns and the actual legal payment schedule require continued monitoring.

segments.name: Family of Apps
segments.text: Revenue was $64.158B and operating income $17.117B. This remains the group’s revenue engine. The legal charge affects the consolidated/segment profit comparison, so raw segment margin should not be treated as a clean advertising efficiency trend without the reconciliation.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.text: Revenue was $443M and operating loss $4.129B. The current revenue base is small relative to the loss. Management expects full-year losses of $18B–$19B; that outlook is a future budget expectation, not a result already recognized for the current quarter.

follow_ups.question: Will advertising growth sustain without the tax-base distortion?
follow_ups.update: Track impressions, price per ad and operating performance rather than headline EPS growth alone.
follow_ups.next_check: Next official quarterly results, filing and relevant supplemental disclosures.

follow_ups.question: Can OCF keep pace with AI infrastructure spending?
follow_ups.update: Retain finance-lease principal in company FCF and compare receipts with the cash investment plan.
follow_ups.next_check: Next official quarterly results, filing and relevant supplemental disclosures.

follow_ups.question: How will legal expenses turn into cash payments?
follow_ups.update: Review settlement obligations, provisions and actual payments separately from new legal proceedings.
follow_ups.next_check: Next official quarterly results, filing and relevant supplemental disclosures.

limitations: Analysis uses the listed official filings, releases and financial attachments; official call text has not been fully reviewed.
Product/geographic categories, reportable segments and adjusted measures retain their disclosed perimeters and must not be double-counted or substituted for consolidated GAAP results.
Cash flows are standalone; cumulative disclosures are differenced across adjacent periods. Issuer adjustments, leases and incentives are identified in metric definitions.
No pre-release consensus snapshot was preserved. Management guidance and analytical inferences are distinct from realized results.

metrics.label: GAAP gross margin
metrics.definition: GAAP gross profit divided by quarterly revenue.

metrics.label: Free cash flow (company definition)
metrics.definition: Company non-GAAP measure: quarterly OCF less equipment purchases and finance-lease principal.
